Use scipy.signal.lfilter with coefficients [alpha, 0] / [1, -(1-alpha)] to create a first-order IIR filter. Estimate local noise from signal differences - high noise means lower alpha (more smoothing), low noise means higher alpha (more responsive). This creates an adaptive filter that automatically adjusts to signal characteristics. The recursive nature ensures minimal computational overhead and low latency. Target the trade-off between lag error (20%) and slope changes (30%) by tuning the noise-to-alpha mapping function.

current_paradigm.idea: Hilbert transform envelope-based adaptive smoothing
current_paradigm.description: Apply scipy.signal.hilbert to compute the analytic signal and extract the instantaneous envelope. Use the envelope to adaptively weight smoothing: apply stronger smoothing when the envelope is low (signal dominated by noise) and weaker smoothing when the envelope is high (strong signal dynamics). This creates a signal-strength-dependent filter that preserves dynamics during strong signal periods while aggressively smoothing during weak/noisy periods. The envelope provides real-time information about signal-to-noise ratio at each sample, enabling truly adaptive filtering that responds to local signal characteristics.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Tracking accuracy and correlation - preserves signal dynamics when strong, reduces noise when weak
current_paradigm.cautions: Hilbert transform works best for narrowband signals. May need to bandpass filter first for broadband signals. Handle edge effects carefully at signal boundaries.

- Multi-sample confirmation (3 consecutive samples) reduces fal...

current_paradigm.idea: Hilbert transform envelope-based adaptive smoothing
current_paradigm.description: Apply scipy.signal.hilbert to compute the analytic signal and extract the instantaneous envelope. Use the envelope to adaptively weight smoothing: apply stronger smoothing when the envelope is low (signal dominated by noise) and weaker smoothing when the envelope is high (strong signal dynamics). This creates a signal-strength-dependent filter that preserves dynamics during strong signal periods while aggressively smoothing during weak/noisy periods. The envelope provides real-time information about signal-to-noise ratio at each sample, enabling truly adaptive filtering that responds to local signal characteristics.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Tracking accuracy and correlation - preserves signal dynamics when strong, reduces noise when weak
current_paradigm.cautions: Hilbert transform works best for narrowband signals. May need to bandpass filter first for broadband signals. Handle edge effects carefully at signal boundaries.

current_paradigm.idea: Use scipy.signal.butter with scipy.signal.filtfilt for zero-phase Butterworth IIR filtering
current_paradigm.description: Design a low-pass Butterworth filter with carefully selected cutoff frequency and order, then apply it using filtfilt for zero-phase filtering. Unlike the current Savitzky-Golay (FIR polynomial) approach, Butterworth IIR provides better frequency characteristics with sharper roll-off. The filtfilt function applies the filter forward and backward, eliminating phase delay entirely. This directly addresses lag error (L_recent and L_avg) which are 40% of the composite score. The filter order and cutoff can be tuned based on the window size and noise characteristics. This is fundamentally different - it uses frequency-domain IIR filtering instead of time-domain polynomial fitting.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Lag error (L_recent, L_avg) and tracking accuracy - the 40% weighted components
current_paradigm.cautions: Butterworth filter design requires proper order selection (too high causes instability, too low causes poor noise rejection). Filtfilt doubles the filter order effectively. Need to handle edge effects carefully. Cutoff frequency must be adaptive based on signal characteristics to avoid over-smoothing rapid legitimate changes.

Combines Savitzky-Golay polynomial smoothing with multi-sample confirmation hysteresis.
Requires consecutive samples exceeding threshold to confirm direction changes,
dramatically reducing false reversals. Uses adaptive smoothing based on trend
confidence and post-processing to smooth minor spurious reversals.

Key improvements:
- Multi-sample confirmation (3 consecutive samples) reduces fal...

current_paradigm.idea: Use scipy.interpolate.PchipInterpolator for monotonicity-preserving piecewise interpolation
current_paradigm.description: Apply PCHIP (Piecewise Cubic Hermite Interpolating Polynomial) to create a smooth signal that preserves monotonicity between data points. Unlike Savitzky-Golay which can introduce oscillations, PCHIP guarantees no spurious extrema between sample points. The approach segments the signal into windows, applies PCHIP interpolation on each segment with controlled derivative constraints, then recombines. This fundamentally reduces slope changes by construction since PCHIP prevents overshoot/undershoot. The smoothness comes from cubic continuity while trend preservation is maintained through local interpolation. This is a fundamentally different mathematical approach from polynomial smoothing - it uses shape-preserving interpolation instead of least-squares fitting.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Slope changes (S) and false reversals (R) - the 60% weighted components of composite score
current_paradigm.cautions: Ensure proper handling of window boundaries to avoid discontinuities. Use appropriate window size (smaller than savgol window for less lag). PCHIP requires careful derivative estimation at boundaries. Test with non-stationary signals to ensure it doesn't over-smooth rapid legitimate changes.

current_paradigm.description: Design a low-pass Butterworth filter with carefully selected cutoff frequency and order, then apply it using filtfilt for zero-phase filtering. Unlike the current Savitzky-Golay (FIR polynomial) approach, Butterworth IIR provides better frequency characteristics with sharper roll-off. The filtfilt function applies the filter forward and backward, eliminating phase delay entirely. This directly addresses lag error (L_recent and L_avg) which are 40% of the composite score. The filter order and cutoff can be tuned based on the window size and noise characteristics. This is fundamentally different - it uses frequency-domain IIR filtering instead of time-domain polynomial fitting.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Lag error (L_recent, L_avg) and tracking accuracy - the 40% weighted components
current_paradigm.cautions: Butterworth filter design requires proper order selection (too high causes instability, too low causes poor noise rejection). Filtfilt doubles the filter order effectively. Need to handle edge effects carefully. Cutoff frequency must be adaptive based on signal characteristics to avoid over-smoothing rapid legitimate changes.

The filtfilt function applies the filter forward and backward, eliminating phase delay entirely. This directly addresses lag error (L_recent and L_avg) which are 40% of the composite score. The filter order and cutoff can be tuned based on the window size and noise characteristics. This is fundamentally different - it uses frequency-domain IIR filtering instead of time-domain polynomial fitting.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Lag error (L_recent, L_avg) and tracking accuracy - the 40% weighted components
current_paradigm.cautions: Butterworth filter design requires proper order selection (too high causes instability, too low causes poor noise rejection). Filtfilt doubles the filter order effectively. current_paradigm.description: Replace current multi-pass smoothing with a single Gaussian filter where sigma adapts to local signal characteristics. Gaussian filter has known frequency response - larger sigma removes more high-frequency noise. Estimate local noise level from signal derivative, then set sigma proportional to noise_std / signal_std ratio. This provides smooth, predictable behavior without the edge artifacts of polynomial filters. Apply the filter once with mode='reflect' to handle boundaries properly. The Gaussian's smooth kernel naturally reduces spurious reversals without the discrete state transitions of hysteresis.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Improve smoothness_score by eliminating the multi-pass smoothing artifacts. Gaussian filter's continuous nature should reduce slope_changes while maintaining responsiveness.

"""
Adaptive Hysteresis with Multi-Sample Confirmation and Savitzky-Golay Filtering

Combines Savitzky-Golay polynomial smoothing with multi-sample confirmation hysteresis.
Requires consecutive samples exceeding threshold to confirm direction changes,
dramatically reducing false reversals. Uses adaptive smoothing based on trend
confidence and post-processing to smooth minor spurious reversals.

Key improvements:
- Multi-sample confirmation (3 consecutive samples) reduces fal...

current_paradigm.idea: Use scipy.signal.detrend with Adaptive Piecewise Linear Fitting
current_paradigm.description: Implement adaptive piecewise linear trend fitting using scipy.signal.detrend in combination with dynamic breakpoint detection. Divide the signal into segments based on local variance, fit linear trends within each segment, and smoothly connect segments. This preserves genuine trend changes (reducing R) while smoothing noise within segments (reducing S). Use scipy.signal.detrend to remove local trends, then reconstruct with adaptive segment lengths based on signal stationarity. This is fundamentally different from polynomial smoothing because it explicitly models trend changes rather than treating them as noise.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: False reversals (R) by preserving genuine trend changes, slope changes (S) by smoothing within trend segments
current_paradigm.cautions: Detect segment boundaries carefully to avoid false reversals, ensure smooth transitions between segments, handle edge cases near segment boundaries, maintain output length constraint

Use scipy.signal.find_peaks for extrema-based trend validation
Use scipy.interpolate.interp1d with piecewise polynomial interpolation

current_paradigm.idea: Use scipy.optimize.minimize for Total Variation (TV) Denoising
current_paradigm.description: Implement Total Variation denoising by minimizing an objective function that combines L2 fidelity to the noisy signal with L1 regularization on the first derivative (slope). This directly targets the slope change penalty (S) and false reversal penalty (R) by penalizing each sign change in the derivative. Use scipy.optimize.minimize with the SLSQP method to solve this constrained optimization problem. The regularization parameter lambda controls the trade-off between smoothness and tracking accuracy - tune it to minimize slope changes while maintaining correlation above 0.1. This approach is fundamentally different from the current Savitzky-Golay + hysteresis method because it optimizes a global objective rather than applying sequential heuristics.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Slope changes (S) and false reversals (R) through L1 derivative regularization, while maintaining tracking accuracy via L2 fidelity term
current_paradigm.cautions: Use multiple starting points to avoid local minima, ensure the objective function is differentiable for SLSQP, tune lambda carefully to balance smoothness vs lag, verify output length matches expected length = n - window_size + 1

The Huber loss downweights large residuals (noise/outliers) while preserving the underlying trend structure. Fit a low-degree polynomial (degree 2-3) over sliding windows, then use the fitted curve as the filtered output. This directly targets reducing false reversals by fitting a smooth trend that ignores noise-induced fluctuations.

current_paradigm.cautions: Implement IRLS manually with scipy.linalg.lstsq (no direct Huber loss in scipy); use moderate polynomial degree (2-3) to avoid overfitting; handle window edges carefully; ensure computational efficiency for real-time processing

current_paradigm.description: Implement a discrete-time Kalman filter using scipy.signal.lfilter to estimate signal states (position and velocity) with adaptive process and measurement noise covariance. Unlike the current EMA-based approach, the Kalman filter provides optimal state estimation with built-in uncertainty quantification. Model the signal as a constant-velocity system where position and velocity evolve over time, with measurements corrupted by noise. The filter naturally balances lag vs. smoothness through the Kalman gain, which adapts based on estimated noise levels. Use the estimated position state as the filtered output. This fundamentally differs by using a principled state-space model rather than heuristic hysteresis.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Minimize lag_error through predictive state estimation; reduce false_reversals through adaptive gain based on uncertainty; improve tracking accuracy via optimal filtering
current_paradigm.cautions: Implement Kalman filter equations correctly (prediction and update steps); tune process noise (Q) and measurement noise (R) covariances based on signal characteristics; handle initialization carefully; ensure numerical stability for long sequences

Model the signal as a constant-velocity system where position and velocity evolve over time, with measurements corrupted by noise. The filter naturally balances lag vs. smoothness through the Kalman gain, which adapts based on estimated noise levels. Use the estimated position state as the filtered output. This fundamentally differs by using a principled state-space model rather than heuristic hysteresis.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Minimize lag_error through predictive state estimation; reduce false_reversals through adaptive gain based on uncertainty; improve tracking accuracy via optimal filtering
current_paradigm.cautions: Implement Kalman filter equations correctly (prediction and update steps); tune process noise (Q) and measurement noise (R) covariances based on signal characteristics; handle initialization carefully; ensure numerical stability for long sequences

current_paradigm.idea: Total Variation Denoising via Sparse Linear System with Slope Constraints
current_paradigm.description: Formulate filtering as a Total Variation (TV) denoising problem that directly minimizes slope changes. Create a sparse linear system Ax = b where A encodes the TV penalty (first differences) and measurement fidelity, then solve using scipy.sparse.linalg.cg (conjugate gradient). Add explicit constraints on maximum slope magnitude to prevent spurious reversals. The TV norm naturally penalizes rapid direction changes while preserving genuine trend transitions. current_paradigm.idea: Use numpy.percentile for rank-based sliding window filtering
current_paradigm.description: Implement a rank-based percentile filter using numpy.percentile with a sliding window approach. Instead of averaging values (mean-based), use the median (50th percentile) or another percentile to filter each window. This is robust to outliers and spikes that cause spurious reversals, fundamentally different from mean-based smoothing. For each position in the signal, compute the percentile of values in the local window and use that as the filtered value. The median naturally suppresses extreme values while preserving the central tendency. After percentile filtering, apply the existing hysteresis confirmation logic to further reduce false reversals. This approach should excel at reducing noise-induced directional changes while maintaining responsiveness to genuine trend shifts.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: S (slope changes), R (false reversals), and smoothness_score - rank-based filtering is inherently more robust to outliers and noise spikes that cause false reversals, while the sliding window maintains local signal characteristics for good tracking
current_paradigm.cautions: Percentile filtering with sliding window is computationally more expensive than mean-based filters - ensure efficiency with vectorized numpy operations. The median introduces its own lag - compensate in output alignment. Edge handling is important - use available samples at boundaries. Test different percentiles (40th-60th) to find optimal trade-off between smoothness and responsiveness.

current_paradigm.description: Apply scipy.signal.wiener with a neighborhood size parameter to perform adaptive smoothing. dramatically reducing false reversals. Uses adaptive smoothing based on trend
confidence and post-processing to smooth minor spurious reversals.

Key improvements:
- Multi-sample confirmation (3 consecutive samples) reduces fal...

current_paradigm.idea: Use scipy.signal.wiener for adaptive local variance-based smoothing
current_paradigm.description: Apply scipy.signal.wiener with a neighborhood size parameter to perform adaptive smoothing. The Wiener filter estimates local variance and automatically applies more smoothing in high-variance (noisy) regions while preserving signal dynamics in low-variance regions. This directly addresses the trade-off between smoothness and responsiveness - noisy sections get smoothed (reducing S and R), while smooth trend sections remain responsive (keeping L_recent low). The filter is computationally efficient and requires no iterative optimization. After Wiener filtering, trim output to match expected length and optionally apply a light derivative threshold to eliminate remaining minor spurious reversals.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Balance between slope changes (S), false reversals (R), and lag error (L_recent) - adaptive smoothing provides context-aware noise reduction
current_paradigm.cautions: Neighborhood size should be odd and related to window_size; Wiener filter may still introduce some lag; ensure proper output length alignment with evaluator's delay calculation

current_paradigm.description: Design a custom FIR low-pass filter using scipy.signal.firwin with a cutoff frequency tuned to the signal characteristics. Calculate an appropriate cutoff frequency based on the window_size (e.g., cutoff = 0.1 / window_size to preserve low-frequency trends while filtering high-frequency noise). Apply the designed filter using scipy.signal.lfilter or scipy.signal.filtfilt for zero-phase filtering. FIR filters provide linear phase response which minimizes phase delay distortion. The key advantage is direct control over the frequency response - we can aggressively filter high-frequency noise (reducing S and R) while preserving the low-frequency signal dynamics (maintaining accuracy). After filtering, trim to expected output length.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Slope changes (S) and false reversals (R) through frequency-domain noise filtering while maintaining tracking accuracy
current_paradigm.cautions: Use firwin with appropriate numtaps (odd number); choose cutoff frequency carefully to avoid over-smoothing; consider using filtfilt for zero-phase but account for increased delay in alignment; verify output length matches evaluator expectations

current_paradigm.description: Implement a custom Kalman filter that models the signal as a state-space system with position and velocity states. Key innovation: adapt the process noise covariance Q based on residual statistics to handle non-stationary signals. This directly addresses false reversals by modeling signal dynamics probabilistically rather than using fixed hysteresis thresholds. The Kalman filter naturally balances lag vs smoothness through the Kalman gain, which adapts based on confidence in the measurement vs prediction.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: false_reversals and slope_changes through probabilistic trend modeling

current_paradigm.description: Implement a Kalman filter with time-varying process noise covariance (Q) that adapts based on innovation (measurement residual) statistics. Unlike the current EMA-based prediction, Kalman provides principled uncertainty quantification. When innovation exceeds expected bounds, increase Q to allow faster tracking of genuine trend changes. When innovation is small, decrease Q to smooth more aggressively. This directly addresses the lag-smoothness tradeoff mathematically rather than heuristically. Use a simple state-space model with position and velocity states. The measurement update reduces lag while the prediction step provides smoothing. Adaptive Q based on residual variance gives the best of both worlds.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Balance lag error (L_recent) and tracking accuracy (L_avg) through principled uncertainty-aware filtering
current_paradigm.cautions: Initialize covariance matrices carefully to avoid divergence, handle edge cases when innovation is zero, tune base Q and R values, ensure state dimensions are appropriate for the problem

Combines Savitzky-Golay polynomial smoothing with multi-sample confirmation hysteresis.

dramatically reducing false reversals. Uses adaptive smoothing based on trend
confidence and post-processing to smooth minor spurious reversals.

Key improvements:
- Multi-sample confirmation (3 consecutive samples) reduces fal...

current_paradigm.idea: Multi-scale derivative analysis with scipy.ndimage.gaussian_gradient_magnitude
current_paradigm.description: Compute gradient magnitude at multiple scales using scipy.ndimage.gaussian_gradient_magnitude to detect genuine vs noise-induced slope changes. At fine scales, noise creates spurious gradients; at coarse scales, only true trends remain. Use the difference between scales to identify and suppress noise-induced reversals. This is fundamentally different from the current single-scale derivative approach. Apply the gradient magnitude to create an adaptive smoothing mask: smooth heavily where multi-scale gradients disagree (likely noise), preserve where they agree (likely signal). This directly targets slope change minimization (S) and false reversal penalty (R) by distinguishing noise from signal in the derivative domain.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Minimize slope changes (S) and false reversals (R) through multi-scale derivative analysis
current_paradigm.cautions: Choose appropriate sigma values for scales (e.g., 1, 2, 4), handle boundary effects, combine scales appropriately to avoid over-smoothing, ensure computational efficiency for real-time processing

current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Reduce false reversals (R) and slope changes (S) while maintaining low lag through edge-preserving denoising
current_paradigm.cautions: Choose appropriate wavelet family (db4/sym4 recommended), apply threshold only to detail coefficients not approximation, ensure reconstruction length matches expected output, may need to trim output to match window_size constraint

current_paradigm.idea: Adaptive Kalman filter with innovation-based noise estimation
current_paradigm.description: Implement a Kalman filter with time-varying process noise covariance (Q) that adapts based on innovation (measurement residual) statistics. Unlike the current EMA-based prediction, Kalman provides principled uncertainty quantification. When innovation exceeds expected bounds, increase Q to allow faster tracking of genuine trend changes. When innovation is small, decrease Q to smooth more aggressively. This directly addresses the lag-smoothness tradeoff mathematically rather than heuristically. Use a simple state-space model with position and velocity states. The measurement update reduces lag while the prediction step provides smoothing. Adaptive Q based on residual variance gives the best of both worlds.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Balance lag error (L_recent) and tracking accuracy (L_avg) through principled uncertainty-aware filtering
current_paradigm.cautions: Initialize covariance matrices carefully to avoid divergence, handle edge cases when innovation is zero, tune base Q and R values, ensure state dimensions are appropriate for the problem

current_paradigm.description: Apply eigenvalue decomposition to a symmetric matrix constructed from the signal's autocorrelation structure to identify and isolate dominant signal components. Create a symmetric Toeplitz-like matrix from the signal where diagonal elements represent signal energy and off-diagonal elements represent temporal correlations. Use eigh to compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors, then reconstruct the signal using only the top k eigenvectors corresponding to the largest eigenvalues. This naturally separates low-frequency trend components (signal) from high-frequency components (noise) without introducing phase lag. The number of retained components k can be tuned based on the window size and expected signal complexity.

Adaptive Hysteresis with Multi-Sample Confirmation and Savitzky-Golay Filtering

Combines Savitzky-Golay polynomial smoothing with multi-sample confirmation hysteresis.
Requires consecutive samples exceeding threshold to confirm direction changes,
dramatically reducing false reversals. Uses adaptive smoothing based on trend
confidence and post-processing to smooth minor spurious reversals.

Key improvements:
- Multi-sample confirmation (3 consecutive samples) reduces fal...

current_paradigm.idea: Use scipy.linalg.eigh for Spectral Decomposition Filtering
current_paradigm.description: Apply eigenvalue decomposition to a symmetric matrix constructed from the signal's autocorrelation structure to identify and isolate dominant signal components. Create a symmetric Toeplitz-like matrix from the signal where diagonal elements represent signal energy and off-diagonal elements represent temporal correlations. Use eigh to compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors, then reconstruct the signal using only the top k eigenvectors corresponding to the largest eigenvalues. This naturally separates low-frequency trend components (signal) from high-frequency components (noise) without introducing phase lag. The number of retained components k can be tuned based on the window size and expected signal complexity.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Slope changes (S) and lag error (L_recent) - spectral filtering preserves signal structure while removing high-frequency noise that causes spurious reversals
current_paradigm.cautions: Matrix construction must be numerically stable; eigenvector selection threshold affects smoothness vs responsiveness tradeoff; ensure reconstruction maintains signal length

current_paradigm.idea: Use scipy.linalg.solve_discrete_are for Optimal Kalman Gain Computation
current_paradigm.description: Implement a Kalman filter where the optimal steady-state gain is computed analytically using solve_discrete_are (Discrete Algebraic Riccati Equation solver) rather than iteratively tuning parameters. Define the state-space model with process noise Q and measurement noise R matrices tuned to the signal characteristics. The solve_discrete_are function computes the optimal Kalman gain K that minimizes the steady-state error covariance, providing theoretically optimal noise reduction. This avoids the iterative tuning that caused previous Kalman filter failures and provides a single-stage optimal solution. The resulting filter has minimal lag while optimally balancing noise reduction and signal tracking.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Lag error (L_recent, L_avg) and false reversals (R) - optimal Kalman gain provides theoretically optimal tradeoff between tracking accuracy and noise suppression
current_paradigm.cautions: Must properly formulate the state-space model matrices A, B, Q, R; ensure numerical stability of Riccati equation solution; handle edge cases where matrices are singular

Create a symmetric Toeplitz-like matrix from the signal where diagonal elements represent signal energy and off-diagonal elements represent temporal correlations. Use eigh to compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors, then reconstruct the signal using only the top k eigenvectors corresponding to the largest eigenvalues. This naturally separates low-frequency trend components (signal) from high-frequency components (noise) without introducing phase lag. The number of retained components k can be tuned based on the window size and expected signal complexity.

current_paradigm.idea: Use scipy.linalg.solve_discrete_are for Optimal Kalman Gain Computation
current_paradigm.description: Implement a Kalman filter where the optimal steady-state gain is computed analytically using solve_discrete_are (Discrete Algebraic Riccati Equation solver) rather than iteratively tuning parameters. Define the state-space model with process noise Q and measurement noise R matrices tuned to the signal characteristics. The solve_discrete_are function computes the optimal Kalman gain K that minimizes the steady-state error covariance, providing theoretically optimal noise reduction. This avoids the iterative tuning that caused previous Kalman filter failures and provides a single-stage optimal solution. The resulting filter has minimal lag while optimally balancing noise reduction and signal tracking.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Lag error (L_recent, L_avg) and false reversals (R) - optimal Kalman gain provides theoretically optimal tradeoff between tracking accuracy and noise suppression
current_paradigm.cautions: Must properly formulate the state-space model matrices A, B, Q, R; ensure numerical stability of Riccati equation solution; handle edge cases where matrices are singular

- Multi-sample confirmation (3 consecutive samples) reduces fal...

current_paradigm.idea: Wavelet Denoising with Soft Thresholding
current_paradigm.description: Apply discrete wavelet transform using db4 wavelets (pywt.dwt) to decompose signal into approximation and detail coefficients. Apply soft thresholding to detail coefficients at multiple scales using universal threshold (sigma * sqrt(2*log(n))). Estimate sigma from median absolute deviation of finest-scale coefficients. Reconstruct signal using inverse wavelet transform. This separates signal from noise in frequency domain, preserving trend changes while removing high-frequency noise that causes false reversals. More principled than frequency-domain filtering for non-stationary signals.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Slope changes and false reversals by removing noise-induced fluctuations while preserving genuine trend changes
current_paradigm.cautions: Choose appropriate wavelet family and decomposition level; soft thresholding is better than hard for smoothness; trim output to expected length; handle edge effects

Estimate process noise Q adaptively based on local signal variance - increase Q when signal is changing rapidly to reduce lag, decrease Q when stable for more smoothing. Measure noise R from local differences. Use standard Kalman equations: predict state using transition matrix, compute innovation, update with Kalman gain. This provides principled Bayesian filtering that naturally balances the lag-smoothness trade-off through the noise covariance parameters, unlike heuristic approaches. The filter is causal and real-time compatible.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Lag error and false reversals through adaptive noise covariance; slope changes through principled smoothing

current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Slope changes and false reversals by removing noise-induced fluctuations while preserving genuine trend changes

Use a sliding window to estimate local noise variance and signal variance, then apply wiener filtering with adaptive window size. The adaptive window adjusts based on local signal complexity: smaller windows for rapid changes, larger windows for smooth regions. This provides optimal linear filtering without the lag of multi-sample confirmation schemes. - Multi-sample confirmation (3 consecutive samples) reduces fal...

current_paradigm.idea: Use scipy.signal.wiener with adaptive noise estimation
current_paradigm.description: Apply scipy.signal.wiener for optimal adaptive filtering that estimates local signal statistics and applies Wiener filtering. The Wiener filter minimizes mean squared error between estimated and true signal. Use a sliding window to estimate local noise variance and signal variance, then apply wiener filtering with adaptive window size. The adaptive window adjusts based on local signal complexity: smaller windows for rapid changes, larger windows for smooth regions. This provides optimal linear filtering without the lag of multi-sample confirmation schemes. Combine with a lightweight directional persistence check that only blocks reversals when the change is below noise threshold.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Reduce L_avg (average tracking error) and L_recent (lag error) while maintaining low slope changes through optimal linear filtering
current_paradigm.cautions: Wiener filter assumes stationary statistics within window - use small enough windows for non-stationary signals. The filter adds minimal lag but may still need a small directional check. Ensure the noise estimate is robust by using median absolute deviation rather than standard deviation.

current_paradigm.description: Separate the signal into trend and noise components using scipy.signal.detrend, then filter each component differently. The trend component (low-frequency, genuine signal changes) is preserved with minimal filtering, while the residual (high-frequency noise) is aggressively filtered. This directly addresses the tracking accuracy metric by ensuring genuine trends are preserved. Implementation: 1) Use detrend with polynomial order to extract baseline trend, 2) Apply aggressive smoothing only to residuals, 3) Reconstruct by adding filtered residuals to original trend. current_paradigm.cautions: Choose appropriate detrend type (linear vs polynomial); ensure trend extraction doesn't remove genuine signal components; handle short signals where detrend may be unstable

current_paradigm.description: Apply scipy.signal.hilbert to compute the analytic signal, extracting instantaneous phase and amplitude. current_paradigm.idea: Use scipy.signal.cwt (Continuous Wavelet Transform) for multi-scale signal decomposition and reconstruction
current_paradigm.description: Apply continuous wavelet transform using scipy.signal.cwt with Morlet wavelet to decompose the noisy signal into multiple frequency scales. Compute the energy at each scale by calculating the mean squared coefficient values. Identify dominant scales by finding scales with energy above a threshold (e.g., 15% of max energy). Reconstruct the signal by keeping only coefficients from dominant scales and zeroing out high-frequency noise scales. Apply inverse wavelet transform to obtain the filtered signal. This approach separates signal from noise based on frequency content rather than slope changes, fundamentally different from the hysteresis approach.
current_paradigm.what_to_optimize: Slope changes (S) and false reversals (R) by removing high-frequency noise components while preserving low-frequency trends
current_paradigm.cautions: Ensure reconstruction produces same length as input; handle edge effects carefully; choose appropriate wavelet (Morlet recommended); scale selection threshold needs tuning based on noise level

Identify the dominant trend scale by computing energy at each scale, then reconstruct the signal using only scales above a threshold that separates noise from signal. The wavelet coefficients can be thresholded (hard or soft thresholding) to remove noise while preserving trend structure.
